gap: No result ChatGPT got states which rear camera, hardwire kit and CPL each under-$200 4K camera takes, with the maker's price for each: 70mai lists the A810S rear cameras as RC24 or RC23 (RC23 'not available yet') and its US 4G kit as UP05 only, while VIOFO's own store has the A119M Pro at $209.99 with the CPL in the box and names it on the $25.99 HK6 listing but not on the $17.99 HK4 listing.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible (cited, read 2026-11-26) and RoadGearLab (cited, read 2026-11-26). Product Bible names the HK6 for A119M Pro hybrid parking but gives no HK6 price, no CPL, no rear-camera compatibility, and quotes only Amazon's $132.99 from Nov 19. RoadGearLab says 70mai parking needs 'its hardwire kit' without naming or pricing it, gives no rear-camera model for the A810S, no CPL, and no card-brand exclusions. Neither states the maker's-store A119M Pro price ($209.99), the RC23/RC24 split, the UP05 US-only 4G limit, or Vantrue's card exclusions. Rivals do hold part of it (HK6 named, 'hardwire kit required'), and the key cells for our own row (Vantrue's kit and rear camera for the S1 Pro Max) could not be opened today, so this is not a 3.
decides: It confirms the picks and adds an add-on cost per row; it does not overturn them. The A119M Pro stays the front-only pick, but it is under $200 only at retailers: VIOFO's US store lists it at $209.99, and parking with voltage cut-off adds the $25.99 HK6 (CPL is already in the box). The 70mai A810S at $139.99 can take only the in-cabin-mounted RC24 rear camera today, since 70mai marks the exterior RC23 'not available yet'; its CPL is a $13.99 extra and its hardwire kit is $27.99 or more. Our Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K + 2.5K sits at $199.99 with the rear camera in its variant name, so any Vantrue hardwire kit ($24.99 to $34.99) takes the parked setup over $200; that should be said in its row. 70mai's older A810 Gift Box (A810 + RC12 rear + hardwire kit + 256GB card + CPL2) is $199.99, the only complete parking-ready 4K kit read at the cap.
